transcript:
Live from NPR News, I'm Dale Willman.
President Trump has praised the arrests of Five Men Sunday in England in connection with
what British authorities are describing as a suspected terror plot.
They were arrested near a British airbase the U.S. has been using to launch attacks
on Iran, and PR's Lauren Frayer reports from London.
The British government declined to join the U.S. in Israeli war on Iran, but it's allowed
the U.S. to use British airbases for what it calls defensive attacks on Iran.
Royal Air Force Base Fairford is one of those, hosting American bombers and reconnaissance
aircraft.
Last summer, Iran's Revolutionary Guard said any base used against Iran is a "legitimate
target."
Early Sunday, police say they intercepted three suspicious vans near RAF Fairford and arrested
five suspects.
They have not identified the men who remain in custody on suspicion, police say, of committing
offenses under the Explosives Act and also of preparing a terrorist act.
Lauren Frayer, NPR News, London.
President Trump says he expects U.S. negotiators to engage in more talks with Iranian officials
this week.
He made his comments in an interview with the news site Axios.
On Friday, Trump rejected the latest plan from Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
Speaking on NBC's Meet the Press, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Arachi says that Iran
is ready if the U.S. takes military action again.
The Wall Street Journal, meanwhile, is reporting that Trump wants to resume bombing in Iran
after the midterm elections in November.
Much of the coast of the Baja Peninsula and other parts of northwest Mexico have been
bracing for Hurricane Polo.
KJZZ's Nina Kravinsky reports from Armosia in Sonora, Mexico.
Hurricane Polo has been making its way north off Mexico's west coast after rapidly intensifying
into a major hurricane.
The storm is expected to make landfall on the Baja Peninsula before making its way inland
to the Mexican state of Sonora across the Gulf of California.
The U.S. Embassy in Mexico warns travelers to be aware of flooding, mudslides, and road
closures early in the week.
The National Hurricane Center says moisture from the hurricane could also lead to heavy
rainfall and flooding in the southwest U.S.
Another storm, Tropical Storm Rachel, off of Mexico's southwest coast has been moving
north in Polo's wake and strengthened into a tropical storm Sunday.
For NPR News, I'm Nina Kravinsky in Hermosillo, Mexico.
The Palestinian death toll from the Hamas-Israel war has now passed 74,000, that's 15,000 more
than the number of Americans who were killed in the Vietnam War.
The latest numbers come from the Gaza Health Ministry.
This is NPR News.
The zoo in Atlanta is welcoming two new giant pandas.
They arrive from China Sunday morning as part of a new agreement between the U.S. and Chinese
governments.
The loan of pandas is part of China's global diplomacy program, and Pearson Wright has
more.
China Pingping, who's six, and female Fu Shuang, who's five, flew in on Boeing's FedEx
Panda Express jet.
The giant pandas will stay in quarantine for about a month in Zoo Atlanta's new Panda complex
before they're introduced to the public on a date to be announced later.
Pingping and Fu Shuang are in Atlanta for 10 years, through a new conservation agreement
between the zoo and the China Wildlife Conservation Association.
China's President Xi Jinping officially confirmed the pandas would soon arrive during his visit
to Washington last week.
Zoo Atlanta is one of three zoos in the U.S. with pandas on loan from China.
Once endangered, they're now classified as a vulnerable species.
Kristen Wright, NPR News.
Avengers and Game Encore landed in first place this weekend at North American theaters, bringing
in $26 million.
It was an encore showing of a movie release seven years ago, but it contains new footage.
It also brought in $60 million in overseas sales.
The reboot of Resident Evil was in second, with $23.3 million in ticket sales, while Heart
of the Beast debuted in third, with $20 million.
Budget flick Primetime finished fourth, bringing in $19.2 million.
The man known as the Calypso King of the World has died.
The family of slinger Francisco, known around the world as "The Mighty Sparrow," says he
died peacefully but released no other details of his death.
He was 91 years old.
His first hit song was released in 1956.
Over his career, he wrote more than 500 songs and recorded 70 albums.
I'm Dale Willman, NPR News.

topics.text: Five men arrested in England in connection with suspected terror plot near RAF Fairford airbase
President Trump expects U.S. negotiators to engage in more talks with Iranian officials this week
Hurricane Polo rapidly intensified into major hurricane, approaching Baja Peninsula and northwest Mexico
Tropical Storm Rachel strengthened into tropical storm off Mexico's southwest coast Sunday
Palestinian death toll from Hamas-Israel war passes 74,000 according to Gaza Health Ministry
Two giant pandas from China arrive at Zoo Atlanta as part of U.S.-China diplomatic agreement
Avengers and Game Encore lands in first place at North American box office with $26 million
Resident Evil reboot takes second place at box office with $23.3 million in ticket sales
The Mighty Sparrow, legendary calypso musician, dies at age 91
